items.title: Why gig workers can’t choose working hours even in extreme weather
items.summary: Even as gig and platform workers form the backbone of several companies that control their incentives, pay and working hours, companies do not have to comply with labour standards for workers’ occupational health, safety or working conditions under India’s labour codes. This makes gig workers more susceptible to extreme climate events, our reporting found. The Code on Social Security defines and includes gig workers, but its implementation is unclear, and the lack of mention of gig workers in the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code (OSH, 2020), puts them at risk of climate impacts on health, productivity and earnings. This is the fourth part of our series on how India’s new labour codes have a climate blindspot, which particularly impacts women workers. You can read the first three parts here , here and here . Ganga (name changed), a 43-year-old gig worker based in Faridabad, is a “partner” with Urban Company. She was first drawn to gig work about a decade ago due to its flexibility of working hours and a decent income. But now, the nature of work has changed. Ganga said Urban Company guarantees a monthly income of Rs 45,000 if they are available for 80 hours on weekdays between 11am and 6pm and on weekends. “I am available for work 6-12 hours a day, including weekends…I typically earn between Rs 30,000-40,000 a month.” The main problem, Ganga said, are gig cancellations. “We are allowed to cancel four bookings in 28 days. If we cross this limit, we will be sent for re-training or access to the app will be paused for a few days,” she said. Previously she had the option of choosing to accept a booking. “Now, we are automatically assigned one, limiting our flexibility.” Ganga works in a 7 km radius around her home, and uses a scooter for commuting. She recalled an incident in May this year when the roads were inundated due to heavy rains. “I raised a ticket for cancellation of a booking. items.title: Kerala High Court refuses to stay State's reconstitution of Waqf Board
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has refused to stay the State government's decision to reconstitute the Kerala State Waqf Board by replacing its existing members with nine newly nominated members. [KS Hamza v State of Keralam & ors and connected case] Justice S Manu passed the order at a special sitting held on Saturday, October 17 to consider two petitions challenging the government's October 16 notification nominating new members to the board. The Court examined whether the government had the authority to cancel the appointments of existing Waqf Board members and nominate new members in their place. It also considered whether the government's decision to replace the existing members was consistent with what it had earlier submitted before a division bench about filling only vacancies on the Board. The Court found that the State government had not acted contrary to the earlier Division Bench orders which had permitted the government to take appropriate steps to ensure that the Board was constituted in accordance with law. " Prima facie, I do not find merit in the submissions made on behalf of the petitioners that reconstitution of the Board is not in accordance with the submissions made before the Division Bench and orders passed in the PILs, " the Court observed. On the question of the government's power to cancel existing appointments, the Court relied on the Supreme Court's judgement in The State of Maharashtra v Shaikh Mahemud & Another which held that the authority to appoint Waqf Board members also included the authority to cancel their appointments. items.title: ‘He can’t tolerate a Dalit moving ahead’: Priyank Kharge targets HD Kumaraswamy
items.summary: Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge on Sunday, October 18, accused Union Minister and Janata Dal (Secular) leader HD Kumaraswamy of resenting the political and social progress of Dalits. The two leaders are engaged in a war of words over a purported sting video involving former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. “If my wearing a suit is intolerable to Kumaraswamy, I will get 10 suits stitched and wear them. If my speaking English is intolerable to him, I will continue speaking English,” Kharge said at a press conference in Kalaburagi. He alleged that Kumaraswamy could not tolerate a Dalit making political progress. A controversy has erupted over a purported video, said to have been recorded in 2023 and recently aired by local television channels. In the reported sting, Siddaramaiah is linked to alleged blackmail and a purported honey-trap network. Kumaraswamy has accused Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar of orchestrating the alleged sting to damage Siddaramaiah’s reputation and force him out of office. Shivakumar has denied the allegation, and the Congress has rejected it. Kumaraswamy has sought an independent probe while accusing the police of targeting JD(S) workers over the video’s circulation. However, Kharge said police should not halt their investigation because some people being questioned were JD(S) members. “Should the police refrain from issuing notices and summoning suspects for questioning just because they are JD(S) activists?” he asked, accusing Kumaraswamy of demanding a probe but objecting when it involved his party’s workers. Kumaraswamy had challenged Kharge to summon him directly instead of detaining JD(S) workers. “If you are a Home Minister, work like one. Issue me a notice if you want, if you have guts,” he said. Kharge also responded to Kumaraswamy’s objection to him and his father, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, contesting from constituencies reserved for Scheduled Castes. He questioned whether society was ready to elect Dalit candidates from general constituencies. Kumaraswamy’s remarks prompted a protest in Mandya on October 17, where Congress workers and Dalit and progressive organisations blocked the old Bengaluru-Mysuru highway and formed a human chain. The protesters accused the Union Minister of making personal attacks on a Dalit leader and warned of statewide demonstrations if the remarks continued.

items.title: BRS sends legal notice to Telugu daily over claims of water diversion to KCR’s farmhouse
items.summary: The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) has sent a legal notice to the Telugu newspaper Velugu, owned by Congress Minister Gaddam Vivek Venkatswamy, over a story alleging that water from the Kondapochamma Sagar Reservoir has been diverted to former Chief Minister K Chandrashekar Rao’s farmhouse in Erravalli village of Siddipet district. Accusing Velugu of publishing a false story against KCR, the BRS legal cell has demanded an unconditional apology to be carried on the front page, warning that the newspaper’s editor and management would otherwise face a defamation suit. The report published in Velugu on October 17 included images of a three-acre well filled with water allegedly part of KCR’s farmhouse. It also showed satellite images of a water body called Panduranga Cheruvu (lake) near the farmhouse spread over 58 acres, alleging that it was completely dry in 2017 but had been filled up with water by 2021 from the Kondapochamma Sagar reservoir, which is part of the Kaleshwaram irrigation project. The report claimed that residents said KCR had the lake dug up around the same time that the reservoir was being built. Velugu alleged that instead of meeting farmers’ irrigation needs, the Kondapochamma Sagar reservoir water was diverted to the lake and from there into a well on the farmhouse premises, all using public funds. items.title: Veeramani POCSO case: Gem Granites manager arrested for helping him evade legal action
items.summary: The Greater Chennai Police (GCP) on Sunday, October 18, arrested Sakthivel, the manager of Gem Granites, for allegedly facilitating financial transactions to help the company’s chairman, R Veeramani, evade legal action in cases involving the alleged sexual abuse of minor girls. The arrest comes amid an ongoing investigation into multiple cases registered against Veeramani under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The police have so far received complaints involving 11 minors and registered seven POCSO cases against him. The latest case was registered on Sunday, based on the statement of another survivor who alleged that she was sexually abused at the residence of Veeramani’s associate Shanthi. According to the police, investigators are examining financial transactions to determine how Veeramani allegedly attempted to evade legal action. As part of the investigation, the police conducted searches at Veeramani’s residence on Lloyds Road in Chennai, his farmhouse in Kanathur, and the office of Chamundeshwari Natural Stone. The investigation began after the Greater Chennai Police’s anti-vice squad received a pen drive containing video evidence allegedly showing sexual offences involving minor girls. Based on the material, Veeramani and his associates Shanti and Mahendra Simhan were arrested on August 29, 2026. Ganesan, another accused, was arrested on September 22 for allegedly possessing another video related to the offences and failing to inform the police about it. Further investigation led to the arrest of three drivers — Lasar, Parthiban and Babu — on October 5, who were allegedly involved in bringing minor girls to locations where Veeramani sexually abused them. All have been arrested and lodged in Puzhal Central Prison and investigators are also searching for N Prakash, a former adviser to the Gem Group of Companies, who is currently absconding. Besides the seven POCSO cases, Veeramani has also been booked in a case relating to the abetment of a minor’s suicide in 2004. With the latest arrest of Sakthivel on Sunday, the total number of arrested persons in the case rises to eight.

items.title: YSRCP withdraws from Punganur municipality polls, alleges TDP violence
items.summary: The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) will not contest the Punganur municipality elections in Andhra Pradesh, citing violence and intimidation by the ruling party. The party said inadequate police security arrangements prevented its candidates from filing nominations before the deadline. Peddireddi Ramachandra Reddy, the party’s MLA from Punganur, announced the decision at a meeting with supporters at his residence in Tirupati on Sunday, October 18. He said YSRCP candidates could not submit their papers without a “free and fair atmosphere” and alleged that rival party workers had used violence while security for his party’s candidates was inadequate. The party failed to file any nominations in Punganur before the 3 pm deadline. YSRCP president and former Chief Minister YS Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the ruling coalition of using intimidation, violence and state machinery to obstruct Opposition candidates. He alleged that police and election officials had not acted impartially. Punganur witnessed violent clashes between the YSRCP and Telugu Desam Party (TDP) members during the nomination process, in which YSRCP MP Midhun Reddy’s convoy was attacked allegedly by TDP cadres. YSRCP MP PV Midhun Reddy moved a house motion petition in the Andhra Pradesh High Court, alleging that officials had refused to accept his party’s nomination papers, and that cases were being filed elsewhere to intimidate its candidates. He said the party was ready to contest and hoped the court would intervene. A Division Bench of Justices Ninala Jayasurya and Chintalapudi Purushottam Kumar dismissed the petition seeking additional time to file nominations. The court said it could not interfere with the election process after the notification had been issued and the stipulated deadline had passed. It asked the State Election Commission (SEC) to clarify its position on a separate request to let candidates who could not file nominations in their local areas submit them at district headquarters. The SEC told the court that extending the deadline was not possible because scrutiny was scheduled for October 19 and the final list of candidates was due on October 21. Polling is scheduled for October 28, with counting on October 30. The court dismissed the petition as having become infructuous. Meanwhile, the police issued notices to Midhun Reddy and Ramachandra Reddy on Sunday morning, asking them not to enter Punganur.
